source: វិធានការចម្រុះគ្រប់គ្រងដំណាំ លើដំណាំស្រូវ (Integrated Pest Management on Rice), training slide deck, Department of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries of Battambang province, presented by Ms. Yem Sophy, Oct 20, 2017 (contact: ysophy168@gmail.com, 012 558 312)
text: Rice thrips (Stenchaetothrips biformis) are a slender, tiny insect common on rice seedlings and young tillers, occurring in both winged and wingless forms. Eggs are laid inside leaf tissue and hatch in about 2-3 days; thrips damage the crop by rasping the still-rolled young leaf surface and sucking the sap that oozes out, leaving the leaf tip curled, yellowed, and dried. A female can lay eggs for roughly 20 days, producing roughly 25 eggs across her lifetime. [The deck states the full egg-to-adult life cycle takes about 3 days; this figure seems unusually fast compared with other regional pest references and should be checked against a primary entomology source before being treated as authoritative.]
